title: Own bug (opt-in autonomy.best_of_n_first_attempt > 1): best-of-N's hand-off to the retry loop broke three state-machine rules. (1) A non-final candidate failure that ends sampling was recorded by handle_attempt_failure, then re-raised into the loop's own handler and recorded again: its budget was charged twice, it was ledgered and progress-classified twice, and role metrics were double-counted. (2) A worktree-reset failure did that too, after the state had already been reset for a candidate that never ran, so the main loop resumed from wiped state and a best_of_n_candidates_tried that raised the global ceiling. (3) Authoritative repair state (sticky API contract recovery, an active MA9 repair contract) survived the independent-candidate reset: the next 'independent' candidate ran in recovery mode, and a verified RESTORE -> REPAIR_BEHAVIOR transition from a non-final candidate was caught as a candidate failure, charged, and the run ended 'recovery budget exhausted before the contract was restored' with the fallback unused (the C6 shape under best-of-N). Fixed: best-of-N hands an already recorded failure to the loop as BestOfNFailureRecorded (the loop acts on its stop decision and never records it again); it stops sampling when the loop must stop, the budgets are spent, or authoritative repair state is active; the fresh sandbox is created before the state is reset; a RecoveryPhaseAdvanced always reaches the loop's own transition handler

title: Product leak (KRIYA_PRODUCT_LEAK): ProcessController.run()/run_async() terminated the spawned tree only on their own timeout; any other exception escaping communicate() (sync) or a cancellation (async) went straight to the containment cleanup with the `docker run` client still alive.
